summary: Add a small, pure-Java risk scoring component in the com.neversoft.sales package that takes a collection of SalesOrders and assigns each an integer risk score from 1 to 10, derived from the order's total value and its number of lines.
approach: The domain model is plain Java objects with no framework, no build file and a dependency-free javac test harness (SalesOrderTest), so the scoring fits as one new stateless class in com.neversoft.sales next to SalesOrder and SalesOrderLine, with no changes to those classes. Order value is the sum of SalesOrderLine.getLineAmount() (a stored, nullable value; null counts as zero) and line count is getLines().size(). Each factor is mapped to a 1-10 sub-score through fixed, documented threshold bands held as constants, and the two are combined into one final score clamped to 1-10. Thresholds are absolute, not relative to the input set, so an order's score is deterministic and independent of the other orders. The result is returned per order, preserving input order, as a small immutable value pairing the order with its score; it is not stored on SalesOrder because that class is equals/hashCode-sensitive and provisional. Null or empty input yields an empty result and a null element is rejected, following the Objects.requireNonNull convention in SalesOrder.addLine. A new dependency-free test class in the existing harness style is run with plain javac and java.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a riskScore field and getter to SalesOrder
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Changes equals/hashCode/toString and the reflection-based structure tests (T-8 to T-18), and stores derived data on a provisional model.

alternatives_considered.option: Score relative to the set (percentile or min-max normalisation)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Scores would shift whenever the set changes and a set of one order would be meaningless; the issue does not ask for relative ranking.

alternatives_considered.option: Continuous formula (for example logarithmic scaling of value) instead of banded thresholds
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Harder to explain, review and test at boundaries; bands are easy to tune later.

alternatives_considered.option: Expose over REST in tools/warehouse-server or in sales-orders-ui
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The issue asks for a way to score orders, not an endpoint or UI; this can be a follow-up.

alternatives_considered.option: Introduce a build tool or JUnit
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Out of scope; the repo convention is the dependency-free harness.

components: com.neversoft.sales scoring component (new) - computes order value and line count, maps each to a 1-10 sub-score through threshold bands, combines them, and returns an ordered list of order/score results for a collection of orders
Risk result value type (new, same package) - immutable pairing of a SalesOrder and its score from 1 to 10
Scoring test harness (new, src/test/java/com/neversoft/sales) - dependency-free tests in the style of SalesOrderTest covering band boundaries, null and empty handling, bounds and ordering
SalesOrder, SalesOrderLine - read only, no changes
assumptions: "Set of sales orders" means any Collection<SalesOrder>, with no uniqueness requirement beyond what the caller supplies.
"Value of each one" means the sum of SalesOrderLine.lineAmount; currency is a single implicit currency as the model has no currency field.
Higher value and more lines both mean higher risk, and 10 is the highest risk.
The deliverable is a library-level capability in the Java domain model, not an API endpoint or UI feature.
Initial threshold bands and the combination rule are reasonable defaults chosen by the implementer and documented in code; they are not business-mandated numbers.
Orders in any status are scored the same way; status is not an input.
Java 25 and no external libraries, per the existing test harness comment.

risks.risk: Thresholds and combination rule are a business decision the issue does not specify, so scores may not match the author's expectation
risks.mitigation: Keep thresholds as named constants in one place, document the rule in Javadoc, and raise it in the open questions for confirmation before merge.

risks.risk: lineAmount is stored rather than derived and may be null or inconsistent with quantity times unit price
risks.mitigation: Use lineAmount as the single source of value, treat null as zero, and state this in the assumptions and Javadoc.

risks.risk: Negative lineAmount (for example credits) could push an order's total below zero
risks.mitigation: Clamp the total at zero for scoring and cover it with a test.

risks.risk: Scoring is a feature with no current caller, so it could drift from future needs
risks.mitigation: Keep the API minimal with no persistence or framework coupling so it is cheap to change.

risks.risk: SalesOrder is mutable and its equals/hashCode are value-based, so using orders as map keys could collapse equal orders
risks.mitigation: Return an ordered list of results rather than a Map<SalesOrder, Integer>.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a collection of SalesOrders, the scorer returns exactly one result per input order, in input order, each with an integer score between 1 and 10 inclusive.
An order's score is derived only from its total value (sum of its lines' lineAmount) and its number of lines.
Holding line count constant, a higher total value never gives a lower score. Holding value constant, a higher line count never gives a lower score.
An order with no lines, or whose line amounts are all null or zero, scores the minimum of 1 and does not throw.
An order with very large value and/or many lines is capped at 10, never above.
Threshold boundaries are defined in one place and documented. Tests cover the value on each side of every boundary, for both factors.
A null or empty collection returns an empty result. A null element in the collection is rejected with a NullPointerException.
A line with a null lineAmount is treated as zero value and does not cause a NullPointerException.
Scoring does not mutate the orders or lines passed in, and a given order's score does not depend on the other orders in the collection.
SalesOrder, SalesOrderLine and Customer are unchanged, and the existing SalesOrderTest still passes.
New main and test code compile with javac --release 25 -Xlint:all -Werror and the new tests run with plain java and exit non-zero on failure.

open_questions: What are the intended value bands (currency amounts) and line-count bands for the 1-10 scale?
How should the two factors be combined: the higher of the two sub-scores, or an average? This plan defaults to the higher, as a conservative risk view, pending confirmation.
Should the score be exposed through the warehouse server or the sales-orders UI in a follow-up?
